newsitem.title: USA: Staunch opponent of de minimis repeal wins office.
newsitem.headline: Staunch opponent of de minimis repeal wins office.

text.p: U.S. Rep. Phil English, R-Pa., a staunch opponent of Clinton Administration efforts to repeal the two-percent "de minimis" rule, narrowly defeated trial attorney Ron Dinicola to win a second House term, his office said.

A member of the powerful House Ways and Means Committee, English helped organize letter-writing campaigns against the Administration's push to end "corporate welfare," including a move to repeal the de minimis rule.
The rule makes it easier for corporations to buy municipal bonds.
English' 51 to 49 percent victory drew a sigh of relief from the Public Securities Association.
"Phil English has show a great deal of leadership on our issues," PSA Executive Vice President Micah Green said in a telephone interview.
"He's someone who, in his short tenure on the Ways and Means Committee, has distinguished himself as someone who cares greatly about issues affecting the bond markets," Green said.
